patch.value: Completion is decomposed while creation is composed: create takes nine inline evidence flags, close takes none, so the prescribed finish protocol is seven invocations and seven unrelated history entries

Measured 2026-08-03 against the shipped surface and the project's own prescribed loop.

The lifecycle is composable at the open end and decomposed at the close end. The create verb accepts nine inline evidence flags: acceptance criteria, comment, dependency, doc, file, learning, note, test, and the acceptance-criteria alias. One invocation can therefore open an item complete with its lineage, its links and its first evidence. The close verb accepts ten flags and not one of them carries evidence: close reason, completed at, author, validate close, resolution, expected result, expected, actual result, actual, force.

The consequence is that the loop the repository prescribes to every agent is seven invocations after the work is done: link files, link docs, link tests, write the evidence comment, run the linked tests, close with a reason, release the claim. Measured per-invocation cost on this tracker is 391 to 442 milliseconds for a small read, against a 66 millisecond floor for a call that short-circuits before dispatch. Six of the seven invocations therefore pay a bootstrap they do not need, and each returns its own receipt, its own envelope metadata and its own row contract to a caller that asked one question: is this work finished and proved.

Three separate costs follow, and only the first is about speed.

First, tokens. Each receipt is independent and none is aware that it is the third of seven, so nothing can elide the metadata blocks the caller has already been served in this sequence.

Second, atomicity. Seven invocations are seven history entries with no transaction identity binding them. A sequence interrupted after the close but before the release leaves a closed item still claimed. A sequence interrupted after the file links but before the close leaves evidence attached to open work that no reader can distinguish from work in progress. The public SDK already ships an atomic multi-item commit primitive and a separate item owns exposing it as a batch surface, but neither makes the prescribed completion sequence itself atomic.

Third, and most important for the stated philosophy, the record cannot say that these seven entries were one act. Project management as context management means a later reader should be able to reconstruct intent, and the intent here is a single one: this is finished, and here is the proof. The record preserves seven unrelated mutations in timestamp order.

This is the write-side mirror of the read-side finding that the prescribed orientation protocol is priced per call and never composes. That item owns the read side. This one owns the write side, and the asymmetry against create is the evidence that the decomposition is incidental rather than designed.

Scope is the completion protocol as one governed act. It is not a proposal for a new noun, and any spelling is subject to the noun-verb decision that governs surface growth.

Finishing an item with links, evidence, resolution and release is expressible as one governed act that costs one bootstrap and returns one receipt; The act is atomic: an interruption leaves either the whole completion recorded or none of it, and no state where an item is closed but still claimed is reachable through the prescribed path; The record identifies the constituent mutations as one act, so a later reader reconstructs the single intent rather than seven timestamp-adjacent entries; The evidence flags accepted at completion are the same names and the same value grammar as the evidence flags accepted at creation, with no second spelling for the same concept; The composed form is never the only form: each constituent verb remains individually callable and unchanged for callers that link evidence incrementally

value.text: Implementation evidence 2026-08-05: commitItemCompletion and pm item complete compose evidence update, governed close, and claim release through one durable compensating transaction. Release is a typed bulk mutation; close/release carry durable markers; forced post-release failure tests prove evidence, lifecycle, and claim ownership restore. CLI contracts, completion discovery, public SDK snapshot, SDK/command docs, integration and packed npm/Bun acceptance are aligned. The intentional BulkItemMutation exhaustive-union change is acknowledged in the calendar-release SDK surface snapshot.

Forward and forced-failure tests prove committed state and exact compensation restoration.
